Recorded here so the exclusion is declared in a machine-readable place rather than only in a code comment.

Named in #520's title. Fix is to add a strict [Thumbnail] lane, which needs a proven-green run first: these cases have never executed in CI, so their pass/fail state is unknown.

PARTIALLY ADDRESSED by #641, which added the GPU-harness 'Integration' batch matching '*Integration*][RequiresGPU]*'. These nine cases carry no [RequiresGPU] tag, so that batch does not reach them and neither does any module lane. #641 fixed the tagged subset and left this one dark.

The headline orphan of #520. run_module_tests.py excludes '*][World][SceneTree]*' from the [SceneTree] lane, which reads as de-duplication against a [World] lane, but no [World] lane exists. The neighbouring [Node]/[Container] exclusions DO dedupe against real lanes, which camouflaged this one. 3 of the 7 carry no [RequiresGPU]; the other 4 were previously credited to the opt-in [requires-RD] catalogue, which blocking CI never runs - so they looked laned while being just as invisible (Codex, PR #658). Adding a strict [World] lane is the fix for the 3, and the 4 need a GPU harness batch; both need a proven-green run.

Same [World] orphan as above, reached through a different tag order ([NodeSurface][World], no [SceneTree]), so a pattern anchored on '[World][SceneTree]' does not cover it. Listed separately to keep each declaration's blast radius visible rather than widening the pattern to '*[World]*'.

unlaned_tests.test_case: [RendererSceneCull] Hidden indexing policy gates Gaussian exemption
unlaned_tests.reason: Gaussian-relevant but lives in the ENGINE test tree (tests/servers/rendering/test_renderer_scene_cull.h), and carries no [GaussianSplatting] tag, so no module lane or GPU batch reaches it. It asserts RendererSceneCull::allows_hidden_visibility_indexing gates the INSTANCE_GAUSSIAN_SPLAT exemption - a real contract on our engine delta. Surfaced only after this guard's corpus scan was widened to the engine tree recursively; a tag-filtered, top-level-only scan missed it. Fix is a lane that reaches gaussian-relevant engine-tree cases, which needs a proven-green run.

Catch-all for [RequiresGPU] cases that no run_gpu_harness.py batch reaches. These were previously credited to REQUIRES_RD_TEST_FILTERS ('GaussianSplatting [requires-RD]'), but _build_module_test_runs() only appends that lane under --gpu / GS_RUN_GPU_TESTS=1 and the blocking workflow (.github/workflows/gaussian_production_gates.yml) invokes the runner without it. That lane's own comment calls itself 'a catalogue of renderer-dependent tests', and it is strict=False even when it does run - so crediting it reported coverage that does not exist (Codex, PR #658). Declared as ONE entry deliberately: the long-term home for GPU deferrals is renderer_release_gate_manifest.json:deferred_requires_gpu_waivers under #329, which is owned elsewhere and currently empty; this entry keeps the cases visible and counted until #329 populates it. The count means a NEW [RequiresGPU] case that no batch reaches still fails this guard. #622 lowered 62 -> 59: the three sort-ORDER oracles in test_gpu_sorting.h were retagged [GpuSort] and now reach the required GpuSorting batch, so they are no longer stranded.
